Compiling other languages

For authors of build packages. Pare's plumbing, the part that puts output under obj/, serves it as a static web asset, publishes it compressed, and deletes it with its source, works for any compile-to-JavaScript step. Husk, which compiles Svelte components, uses it. If you only write TypeScript you can skip this page.

Declare the sources and your target

Usually in your package's .props and .targets:

XML 
<ItemGroup>
  <PareCompileSource Include="Components/**/*.svelte" PareCompiler="husk"
                     PareOutputExtension=".svelte.js" PareServeAt="/" />
</ItemGroup>
<PropertyGroup>
  <PareCompileDependsOn>$(PareCompileDependsOn);HuskCompile</PareCompileDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
<Target Name="HuskCompile" Inputs="@(PareCompileSource)" Outputs=&quot;@(PareCompileSource->'%(PareOutputPath)')">
  <!-- write each source's output to %(PareOutputPath) -->
</Target>
Metadata
PareCompiler required: the compiler's name, the same as its IPareCompiler.Name
PareOutputExtension required: the output's name is the source's name without its extension, plus this (App.svelte + .svelte.js = App.svelte.js)
PareServeAt as for TypeScriptSource
  • Targets in PareCompileDependsOn run inside PareStripTypeScript, after the strip and before the outputs are registered. Each @(PareCompileSource) then has PareOutputPath (where to write; relative paths are below the project) and PareRelativePath (its URL or resource name). Skipping up-to-date sources is the target's job (Inputs/Outputs).
  • Two outputs from one source (a component's .js and .css) are two items with the same Include and different extensions. Every file the target writes under obj/ must be one of these outputs: the build deletes any other file there as a deleted source's output (a .js.map it was not told about, say).
  • The sources leave Content, so a .svelte under wwwroot is not published. They are Watch items. @(PareOutput) lists their outputs, with %(PareCompiler).
  • error PARE204 for a missing PareCompiler (letters, digits, ., _, -) or PareOutputExtension. PARE201, PARE202 and PARE203 apply as for TypeScript, across both kinds of source.

Hot reload

On save in Development, AddPareDevelopment() hands each such source to the IPareCompiler with its name, registered in DI:

C# 
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IPareCompiler, SvelteCompiler>();
builder.AddPareDevelopment();   // a second call, from another package's setup, adds no watcher; its options apply too

CompileAsync(sourcePath, source, outputPaths, logger, cancellationToken) returns the text of each output keyed by path, or null after logging its errors (the old outputs stay). Pare calls each compiler one source at a time, writes what changed and deletes the outputs of a deleted source. Sources out of date at start are compiled before the app serves. A source whose compiler is not registered gets a warning at start and is not compiled.

The decision behind this is decision 005 (docs/decisions/ in the repository).
